I will keep my land in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the steadiest way for me to make use of the whole year, and at my age I would rather do something familiar, proven, and manageable than spread myself across too many crops. At the start of this season, my winter wheat is already in the field from last autumn, so I will focus on feeding it well, watering it at the key stages, and controlling weeds and aphids if they show up. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize on the same land, using improved seed, enough fertilizer to keep the stand strong, fewer but timely irrigations, and basic pest control. I will not make the plan complicated. I will stay with grain crops I know, keep costs under control, and aim for stable yield instead of chasing something risky.
